questions.question: Walk me through a dataset you cleaned. What problems did you find, and how did you check your result?
questions.tip: Name one real dataset (it can be from a course or a personal project). Describe one check you did, such as duplicates or missing values.

questions.question: Explain a chart or result you made to someone without a technical background.
questions.tip: Start with the question it answered, then the main finding in one sentence. Say what you did not know.

questions.question: Tell me about a time your analysis or code was wrong. What happened next?
questions.tip: Focus on how you found the error and what you changed afterwards. Honesty about mistakes is a strength.

questions.question: How do you decide whether data is good enough to use?
questions.tip: Mention concrete checks: source, completeness, recency, and whether it fits the question.

questions.question: Describe a project you built. What would you do differently now?
questions.tip: Pick a small project you can explain fully. Name one improvement you would make.

questions.question: How would you explain the limits of an AI or machine-learning result to a manager?
questions.tip: Talk about uncertainty, what the data does not cover, and how a person stays responsible for the decision.

questions.question: How do you keep personal data safe in your work?
questions.tip: Mention examples such as using invented or anonymised data, access rights, and not pasting personal data into public tools.

questions.question: Which tool in this advert are you still learning, and what is your plan?
questions.tip: Be honest about the gap. Give your first concrete step and when you will take it.
